name: Chkobba
description: Chkobba is a Tunisian and Algerian fishing card game closely related to the Italian game Scopa. Players capture cards from the table by matching values or making combinations that sum to the played card's value. The game is traditionally played with a 40-card Spanish deck and features the same core mechanics as Scopa, including scoring for the most cards, most coins/diamonds, the seven of coins (settebello), and achieving sweeps (chkobba).

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Tunisia and Algeria
Time Period: 19th-20th century
Historical Development: Brought to North Africa by Italian migrants, Chkobba evolved from the Italian game Scopa. The game became deeply embedded in Tunisian and Algerian culture, with local variations developing over time.
Cultural Significance: Chkobba is more than a game in Tunisiaâ€”it is a social tradition often played in cafes, at family gatherings, and during celebrations. The game represents a cultural bridge between North Africa and Mediterranean Europe.
timeline: 19th century: Italian migrants bring Scopa to North Africa
Early 20th century: Chkobba develops as a distinct variant in Tunisia and Algeria
Mid-20th century: Game becomes firmly established in North African culture
Present day: Remains popular in Tunisia, Algeria, and among diaspora communities
history.cultural: In Tunisia, Chkobba is traditionally played in cafes and social gatherings. The game is often accompanied by tea and conversation, serving as an important social activity. Terra Delyssa, a Tunisian olive oil brand, has even used Chkobba in marketing campaigns to connect with cultural heritage.
history.evolution: Chkobba evolved from Italian Scopa, adapting to local preferences and using Spanish-style cards common in the region. The core mechanics remained similar, but local scoring conventions and customs developed.

rules.objective: Score points by capturing cards from the table and achieving specific combinations. The game is typically played to 11 points (or 21 points in some versions), with points awarded for most cards captured, most cards in the coins/diamonds suit, holding the seven of coins (settebello), and achieving sweeps (chkobba).
rules.gameplay:
1. Initial deal: 3 cards to each player, 4 cards face-up on table
2. If 2+ Aces on table, reshuffle and redeal
3. Players take turns counterclockwise playing one card
4. Capture by matching a table card's value OR by playing a card whose value equals the sum of multiple table cards
5. Captured cards are stored face-down in trick piles
6. When all players have played their 3 cards, dealer deals 3 more cards to each player (no more table cards)
7. Continue until all cards are played
8. Last player to capture takes remaining table cards
keyRules: Must capture if possible - cannot play a card that could capture without capturing
If a card can capture in multiple ways, player chooses which capture to make
When table cards sum to the played card's value, all those cards are captured together
A sweep (chkobba) occurs when a play captures all cards on the table, leaving it empty
The card used to make a sweep is turned face-up in the trick pile to mark the sweep
Last player to capture any cards takes remaining table cards at end of round

strategy.basic: Focus on capturing high-value cards, especially the seven of coins (settebello). Try to maintain cards that can capture multiple table cards. Avoid leaving easy captures for opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards to track what has been played, especially the coins suit. Set up sweeps by leaving table combinations that you can capture on your next turn. Balance capturing cards now versus setting up future captures.
strategy.advanced: Use tactical plays to force opponents into unfavorable positions. Control the tempo to ensure you get advantageous final captures. Track opponent patterns to predict their holdings. Set up situations where any card an opponent plays can be captured.
tips: Always be aware of the seven of coins - it's worth a full point
Try to capture the majority of coins suit cards early
Setting up a sweep (chkobba) can swing the game significantly
Remember which high cards have been played to predict opponent options
Sometimes it's better to play a low card that doesn't capture to set up future plays
